policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the participle actively, 'the Levites that taught all Israel', which is the hiphil הַמְּבִינִים 'those causing to understand, instructing'. The ketiv המבונים is a passive/polal-shaped form ('those instructed'), which the ASV wording excludes; no ASV note is mapped here.

Qere and ketiv differ only in the orthography of the personal name (וְכָנַנְיָהוּ vs. וכונניהו); ASV 'Conaniah also' transliterates either equally, and no ASV note is mapped to this unit, so the English does not distinguish the readings. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
